For the second labeling procedure, dissolve the QC-1 dye in 125 μL of ultrapure water to obtain a concentration of 4 μg/μL. Vortex the solution for 10 s and rapidly add 2.49 μL of the QC-1 solution to 100 μL of purified antibody solution. Note: The QC-1 dye is based on an NHS-ester formulation, which is unstable at the moment of solvation. Critical step: Use QC-1 within 2–3 h after solvation to ensure labeling efficiency. Incubate protected from light at 20 °C in the Thermo Mixer C for 2 h. a. The 2.49 μL of QC-1 dye solution is a variable volume and depends on the volume of antibody solution that has been labeled. In the following, we demonstrate the calculation for an example of a 100 μL purified antibody solution: i. 100 μL of purified solution + 10 μL of 1 M sodium bicarbonate = 110 μL sample. ii. The QC-1 dye manufacturer’s volume value is based on 1,000 μL of protein solution. The factor for 100 μL is 10 (see step A7a.v). iii. Calculate the volume of QC-1 using its molecular weight of 1243.7 [g/mol]/150 [kDa] (antibody) = 8.291 μL. Note: The conversion of the result to μL is given by the manufacturer. iv. Calculate the volume value by the factor = 8.291 μL/10 = 0.8291 μL. v. The QC-1 dye should be used at a dilution of 1:3, which is 0.8291 μL × 3 = 2.49 μL.

steps.title: Prepare antibody for labeling
steps.instruction: Select the antibody to be labeled (e.g., HA‑tag ab49969) and ensure it is at 1 mg/mL in a glycine‑free buffer; if the stock contains glycine, dialyze before proceeding.

steps.title: Desalt antibody with Zeba columns
steps.instruction: Remove BSA and other peptides using Zeba spin desalting columns (7 kDa MWCO, 75 µL).

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge two columns at 1,500 × g for 1 min to discard storage solution.
Wash resin three times with 300 µL PBS, centrifuging at 1,500 × g for 1 min each wash.
Load the antibody onto the column center and centrifuge at 1,500 × g for 2 min into a 1.5 mL LoBind tube.

steps.title: Measure antibody concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the purified antibody concentration with a Nanodrop 8000 using the Protein A280 menu; adjust to exactly 1 mg/mL if necessary.

steps.title: Adjust pH for labeling
steps.instruction: Dilute the antibody 10:1 with 1 M sodium bicarbonate and verify the pH is 8.5 using pH‑indicator strips (0.5 µL per strip).

steps.title: Label with Alexa Fluor 680
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 1 mg/mL antibody to a vial containing solid Alexa Fluor 680 dye, dissolve gently, and incubate protected from light at 20 °C in a Thermo Mixer C for 1 h.

steps.title: Label with QC‑1 quencher
steps.instruction: Prepare QC‑1 solution at 4 µg/µL by dissolving the dye in 125 µL ultrapure water, vortex 10 s, then add 2.49 µL to 100 µL antibody (calculated as described) and incubate protected from light at 20 °C for 2 h; use within 2–3 h of solvation.

substeps.instruction: Calculate QC‑1 volume: for 100 µL antibody + 10 µL 1 M bicarbonate = 110 µL total.
Manufacturer factor for 1,000 µL is 1; for 100 µL use factor 10.
Molecular‑weight based volume = 8.291 µL; divide by factor 10 → 0.8291 µL.

steps.title: Resuspend labeling reactions
steps.instruction: Gently vortex each labeling reaction every 15 min during incubation.

steps.title: Purify labeled antibodies
steps.instruction: Remove free dye using spin‑column purification resin according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

substeps.instruction: Add resin to a 5 mL screw‑cap tube and centrifuge at 1,100 × g for 10 s (Rotina 420R).
Repeat until the column is packed with resin.
Pack the column by centrifuging at 1,100 × g for 4 min.
Load each labeled antibody onto separate columns, collect flow‑through into a LoBind tube, and centrifuge at 1,100 × g for 5 min.
Elute each antibody a second time, collect into a 0.5 mL LoBind tube, and repeat the 5 min centrifugation.

steps.title: Determine labeled antibody concentration
steps.instruction: Measure each purified labeled antibody in technical triplicate on the Nanodrop 8000 (Protein A280 menu) and calculate mean concentration using Equation 1.

steps.title: Measure degree of labeling
steps.instruction: In triplicate, record absorbance at 280 nm and at λmax (679 nm for 680 nm dye or 750 nm for QC‑1) using the UV‑VIS menu; compute mean degree of labeling with Equation 2.

steps.title: Add BSA if concentration low
steps.instruction: If the labeled antibody concentration is <1 mg/mL, add 1 µL of 100 mg/mL BSA stock to the solution.

steps.title: Adjust pH and store antibodies
steps.instruction: Check pH to 7.2 with indicator strips, then store labeled antibodies protected from light at 4 °C.

steps.title: Calculate labeling success
steps.instruction: Apply manufacturer‑provided correction factors (λmax and ε) and use 2 030 000 in Equation 1; multiply ε by 10 as instructed; verify results fall within the specified successful range.

steps.title: Prepare diluted antibody for FLISA
steps.instruction: Multiply the mean concentration obtained in step 12 by 200 to obtain the volume of diluted antibody needed for the 1:200 primary‑antibody dilution in the assay.

steps.title: Prepare coating solutions
steps.instruction: Make two coating buffers: alpha‑bungarotoxin and alpha‑bungarotoxin‑Biotin‑XX each at 20 µg/mL in ELISA phosphate coating buffer (10 mM phosphate, pH 7.4).

steps.title: Coat microplate with bait protein
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the appropriate coating solution to each well of a black 96‑well clear‑bottom plate according to the layout (columns 1A,B,F–H,5–11A–H,12A–C,G,H for alpha‑bungarotoxin; columns 2–4A–H for alpha‑bungarotoxin‑Biotin‑XX).

substeps.instruction: Incubate the coated plate overnight at 4 °C on a Varioshake set to 50 rpm.

steps.title: First FLISA run – wash plate
steps.instruction: Wash each well twice with 150 µL 0.1 % PBST for 5 min each, then once with 150 µL PBS.

steps.title: First FLISA run – block wells
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL blocking buffer to each well and incubate 1 h at room temperature with shaking at 150 rpm on a KS 260 control IKA.

steps.title: First FLISA run – add protein sample
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL purified α1 2 β1δε or α7 nAChR sample (≤0.1 mg/mL) to each well.

steps.title: First FLISA run – bind sample
steps.instruction: Incubate 1 h at room temperature with shaking at 150 rpm (KS 260) to allow α‑subunit binding to the bait protein.

steps.title: First FLISA run – wash again
steps.instruction: Repeat the washing procedure from step 9 (two 5‑min PBST washes, one PBS wash).

steps.title: First FLISA run – primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL per well of the appropriate primary‑antibody dilution (1:200 in blocking buffer) and incubate 30 min at room temperature, 150 rpm (KS 260).

steps.title: First FLISA run – secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: After washing as before, add 100 µL per well of the designated secondary‑antibody dilution and incubate 1 h at room temperature, protected from light, shaking at 150 rpm (KS 260).

steps.title: First FLISA run – final wash and scan
steps.instruction: Wash plate again, add 100 µL PBS to each well, then scan the plate with the Odyssey CLx using Image Studio settings: resolution = 169 µm, quality = medium, focus offset = 3.8 mm.

steps.title: First FLISA run – export data
steps.instruction: Export fluorescence data as an Excel report.

steps.title: Second FLISA run – primary antibody
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL per well of the second‑run primary‑antibody dilution and incubate 30 min at room temperature, 150 rpm (KS 260).

steps.title: Second FLISA run – secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash, then add 100 µL per well of the second‑run secondary‑antibody dilution and incubate 1 h at room temperature, protected from light, 150 rpm (KS 260).

steps.title: Second FLISA run – scan and export
steps.instruction: Wash, add PBS, scan with the Odyssey CLx (same Image Studio settings), and export the data as an Excel file.

steps.title: Third FLISA run – primary antibody only
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL per well of the third‑run primary‑antibody dilution, incubate 30 min at room temperature, 150 rpm (KS 260), then wash.

steps.title: Third FLISA run – scan and export
steps.instruction: Add PBS, scan the plate with the Odyssey CLx (same settings), and export the results as an Excel report.

steps.title: Run negative‑control FLISA
steps.instruction: Repeat steps B1 through B4 (coating, overnight incubation, wash, block, sample addition, binding, washes, primary and secondary incubations, scanning) in a separate 96‑well plate using protein lysate from non‑transgenic CHO cells as the sample.
